DRAFT MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA
  October 9, 2012

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was called to order
this day at 7:00 PM in the Council Chambers of City Hall by Mayor Bird.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEM(S)

CLOSED SESSION

CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT

City attorney Hogin 7;00pm Council recessed to Closed Session; items on agenda were discussed
as posted. She said for several decades City has had possession of these homes; providing a brief
history, beginning with an assertion that a storm drain had caused erosion. Plaintiff was awarded
$1.9 million; new storm was installed to divert water from the bluff area. Settlements were made
with homeowners of 10 properties along the bluff - some with life estats; others were taken
ownership of. Recently, the City has come into the ownership of all 10 properties. Concerns were
voiced regarding vacancies of the homes, but it was known that teh properties could not be sold
because it was in a landslide area. The City decided reports to assess the properties; the homes were
made to availalbe to City employees with preference to front line and key staff. Over time, there
has been turnover and through attrition alot of these homes are now vacant; and the homes have
degraded. being on unstable land, maintaining them was questionable. Council has evaluated these
properties, watch on geology, cracks and continued land movement; some have more significant
issues. A geologist loked at current state with results that slow creep continues; part of findings
included that some of the properties are subject to catastrophic failure due to the height of the
bluff. The County Tax Assessor possessory interest tax owed on the property has not been paid.
Council has decided to not rent the properties any longer. None of occupants have been involved in
discussion or Closed Session discussions. City Council authorized offers to settle any claims that
the occupants might have with regard to taxes or conitnued occupancy of the homes. Entered into
agreement with City Manager; CC will pay $25,000 lump sum to cover expenses with sudden
disruption of license agreement. Employment Agreement afforded additional cash salary in lieu of
in kind benefit; in exchange for which she will vacate by January 31, 2013; a release will be
signed. Also entered into agreement with Allan Rigg; agrement with CAA, which accounts for
occupany of the home. $25,000/yr. credit will no longer be in force. Same release shall be
provided by the City. The same offer has been made to the Chief of Police as was offered to the
City Manager. She said they have not discussed what shall be done with the properties, structures,
or uses, which shall be discussed in Open Session.

Mayor Bird said each fo the 3 agreements were different; standardized to the end fo January.
TheCity owned 10 properties; teh geologyc reports are all public records to be made available to
the public.
